Maps Show How a Glacier Collapse Triggered Deadly Nepal Floods

2026-08-28 NBC News glacier collapse, Nepal, Tibet, flash flood, satellite imagery, disaster mapping, Himalaya, climate change
Read the source article

Quick summary

NBC News uses maps and satellite imagery to trace the glacier collapse and floodwaters that devastated communities along the Nepal-Tibet border, killing over 380 people with hundreds more missing.

Key takeaways

  • Over 380 people have died and hundreds more are missing since catastrophic flash flooding tore through villages along the Nepal-Tibet border on August 26, 2026
  • Over 600 foreigners are missing, including 65 Americans, according to the Nepal Tourism Board
  • Maps and satellite imagery trace the glacier collapse and the path of floodwaters downstream
  • The disaster affected remote mountain communities along the Nepal-China border
  • The event represents one of the deadliest glacier-related disasters in recent Himalayan history
